titulo: What if China invaded Taiwan today?

lines.t: About *130 kilometers* of sea separate China from Taiwan.
lines.say: About a hundred and thirty kilometers of sea separate China from Taiwan.

lines.t: And they could decide the *future of the planet*.
Since *1949*, Taiwan has governed itself separately.
lines.say: Since nineteen forty-nine, Taiwan has governed itself separately.

lines.t: *Beijing* considers it part of China and does not rule out using *force*.
Why does it matter so much? Because of this:
Taiwan makes *over 90%* of the world's *most advanced* chips.
lines.say: Taiwan makes over ninety percent of the world's most advanced chips.

lines.t: Your *phone*, your *car*, *artificial intelligence*... they all depend on this island.
Suppose China decides to *invade*.
First would come a *blockade*: ships and missiles surround the island and trade stops.
Then, the largest *amphibious* operation since *Normandy*:
hundreds of ships crossing the strait under enemy fire.
But Taiwan is a *natural fortress*:
mountains, few suitable beaches, and seas so *rough* they can only be crossed at certain times of year.
If the *United States* and *Japan* step in, the war goes global.
In 2023, the think tank *CSIS* simulated this war *24 times*.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-three, the think tank C S I S simulated this war twenty-four times.

lines.t: In most of them, the invasion *failed*... but with dozens of ships and hundreds of aircraft *lost*.
According to *Bloomberg Economics*, global GDP could drop by about *10%*.
lines.say: According to Bloomberg Economics, global G D P could drop by about ten percent.

lines.t: A bigger hit than the *2008* crisis and the *pandemic*.
lines.say: A bigger hit than the two thousand eight crisis and the pandemic.

lines.t: In this war, probably *nobody would win*.
Do you think it will *ever happen*? Tell me in the comments.
